City of Commerce

  Meeting Minutes

CALL TO ORDER

PUBLIC COMMENT

Yvonne Sandoval, President of Senior Club at the Senior Center, provided an
update on the senior center trips. A trip was scheduled for the end of March and
there were still seats available. April 4 and April 10 are the dates for the senior
trips for the month of April. She also expressed her gratitude to the Council for the
arts classes at the senior center with the world-famous artist Calixto.

Leslie Navarro, Representative of the Helpline Youth Counseling Non-Profit
Organization and the Southeast Community Alliance Coalition (SECA) Lets Make
a Difference Campaign, provided information on a community level prevention
effort focused on reducing alcohol, drug, and prescription medication use across
Los Angeles. The goal was to educate families to safely store and dispose of
medication. They work with pharmacies, schools and several organizations to
provide these services. She stated that Commerce did not have a location to safely
dispose of these medications. Ms. Navarro requested to collaborate with the City
to provide this information at their City events and for the City to register and
participate in the National Take Back Day on April 25, 2026.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

Council Member Argumedo removed Item No. 3 for separate discussion.
Council Member Argumedo moved, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Garcia to
approve Item Nos. 1, 2, 4, 5, 6. The motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes:  5-  Mayor Lainez, Mayor Pro Tem Garcia, Councilmember Altamirano, Councilmember Argumedo, and
  Councilmember Rebollo

1.  Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 13A, 13B, 13C, and 13A S/A

Action Taken: Approved the bills and claims set forth in Warrant Registers
No. 13A dated March 10, 2026, 13B for the period of February 25, 2026
through March 4, 2026, 13C for the period of February 19, 2026 through
February 23, 2026, and 13A S/A dated February 19, 2026.

2.  Approval of Minutes

Action Taken: Approved the minutes of the Regular City Council meeting of
Tuesday, February 24, 2026, held at 5:00 p.m.

City of Commerce  Page 3  Printed on 5/13/2026
 City Council  Meeting Minutes  March 10, 2026

3.  Adoption of a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the Agreement with
  Flock Safety to Modify and Expand Services for Mobile Security Camera
  Trailers
Council Member Argumedo removed this item for separate discussion.

Council Member Argumedo inquired if the issues with the previous company were
resolved with this company. He would like to see a long term resolution on this
item.

City Manager Hernandez affirmed that these issues were resolved. These units
were used at hot spots throughout the City. Staff was working on other viable
solutions.

Council Member Argumedo requested that staff provide a six month report update
on the use of these cameras.
Council  Member  Argumedo  moved,  seconded  by  Council  Member
Altamirano to Adopt a Resolution No. 26-13 approving the First Amendment
to the existing agreement with Flock Safety, previously approved by the
City Council on November 25, 2025, to expand services to include mobile
security camera trailer rentals for a 12-month period to better support the
City's public safety objectives and ensure reliable, high-quality surveillance
capabilities.

The motion carried by the following vote:

4.  FY 2025-26 Mid-Year Budget Amendments

Action Taken: Approved the Mid-Year budget amendments  for  the  fiscal
year (FY) 2025-26 General Fund Budget as outlined in this report.

5.  Annual Financial Comprehensive Report  and  the  Auditor’s  Communication
  Related to Fiscal Year 2024-25 Annual Audit
Action Taken: Received and filed the Annual Comprehensive Financial
Report (ACFR) for the Fiscal Year (FY) ended June 30, 2025, and accept the
report as presented by the city’s independent auditors, The Pun Group, LLP.

6.  Adopt a Resolution Approving a Fund Trade Agreement for the Exchange of
  Proposition A Funds with the City of Lomita
Action Taken:  Adopted Resolution No. 26-14 approving a Fund  Trade
Agreement for the exchange of Proposition A funds with the City of Lomita.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

7.  Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department of Public Safety in the City
  of Commerce
Sergeant Cortez provided a presentation on this item.

8.  Expansion of Public Wi-Fi Access (Phase I)

Mayor Lainez moved, seconded by Council Member Rebollo to:

1.  Approve an agreement with Southern Computer Warehouse for a
not-to-exceed amount of $27,000 for wireless access points, licensing, and
mounting hardware.
2.  Approve an agreement with Integrated Security for a not-to-exceed
amount of $14,000 for cabling and installation at park facilities
3.  Authorize the City Manager to execute all contracts, in a form approved
by the City Attorney.
4.  Adopt Resolution No. 26-15 appropriating $41,000 from the Project
Management Fund to support the one-time cost for the Phase I of the
project.

The motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes:  5-  Mayor Lainez, Mayor Pro Tem Garcia, Councilmember Altamirano, Councilmember Argumedo, and
  Councilmember Rebollo

City of Commerce  Page 5  Printed on 5/13/2026
 City Council  Meeting Minutes  March 10, 2026

9.  Proposed Independence Day Celebration Program - July 3-4, 2026

Director of Parks & Recreation  Marquez  provided  a  brief  summary  of  the
PowerPoint Presentation for this Item.

Council Member Rebollo requested clarification on the music selection. She would
like the music selection to be inclusive of all generations.

Council Member Argumedo followed up on getting the fireworks on the 4th of July,
was there anything prohibiting the City to work on this issue now to secure that in
the future. He asked how the drone show was received from the community. He
also suggested a mini parade for the event.

Director Marquez stated that the five firework vendors have heard from the City for
two years now every few months and in January staff begin monthly calls to try to
get the fireworks on the 4th of July. The City was in line for this programming.
Director Marquez stated they heard very positive comments on the drone show.
The laser light show also had received positive feedback from the teenagers and
all age ranges.

City Manager Hernandez stated that in May Contract Cities were going to meet
with a subdivision of TNT to create another company that provided this service.
Unless existing cities change their programming on their 4th of July events,
Commerce was in line to be scheduled for the 4th. This item today would establish
the budget for the two day event and the programming for day two is where Council
can be creative.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia inquired if the City received a discount on the fireworks
show since it is on July 3rd and when did the City stop being scheduled for the 4th.

City Manager Hernandez stated that the fireworks shows are more expensive on
July 4th.

Director Marquez stated that after Covid, it was decided that the 4th of July was
going to be celebrated the weekend before. The City chose to get out of the line for
the 4th of July programming and these are the residual effects of that decision.

Mayor Lainez stated that the drone show was a good idea but the laser light show
was really lively and gave a concert experience, a lot of people got into it and

City of Commerce  Page 6  Printed on 5/13/2026
 City Council  Meeting Minutes  March 10, 2026

enjoyed it. Being that the City does not have a fireworks show on the 4th, the laser
light show is a good main event for the 4th. We can also look at having a drone
show. He was concerned with the smoke from neighborhood fireworks impairing
the visibility of the drone show.
Mayor Lainez moved, seconded by Council Member Rebollo to:

Approve the  two-day (Friday, July 3 and Saturday, July 4, 2026)
Independence Day Celebration events as listed in the staff report in the
amount $305,244, this funding was approved in the mid-year budget
amendments.

The motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes:  5-  Mayor Lainez, Mayor Pro Tem Garcia, Councilmember Altamirano, Councilmember Argumedo, and
  Councilmember Rebollo

  ORDINANCES

10.  Adoption of Ordinance No. 830 Authorizing an Amendment to the City’s
  CalPERS Contract to Provide Up to Two (2) Years of Additional Service Credit
  (“Golden Handshake”) and Adoption of an Urgency Ordinance Authorizing the
  Same Amendment
Human Resources Manager Reviilla provided a brief summary on this item.
Council  Member  Rebollo  moved,  seconded  by  Council  Member  Altamirano
to:

1.  Adopt Ordinance No. 830, previously introduced on February 10, 2026,
authorizing an amendment to the contract between the City Council of the
City of Commerce and the Board of Administration of the California Public
Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS).

2. Adopt Urgency Ordinance No. 832, authorizing the same amendment to
the CalPERS contract to allow the amendment to take effect immediately
upon adoption.

The motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes:  5-  Mayor Lainez, Mayor Pro Tem Garcia, Councilmember Altamirano, Councilmember Argumedo, and
  Councilmember Rebollo

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS

Council Member Rebollo had no reports.

Council  Member  Altamirano  congratulated  Council  Member  Argumedo  on
receiving the George Tumanjan Philantropic Award from the Chamber of
Commerce on Thursday, March 5, 2026. He provided an update on Art projects
around the City, the green container by the baseball fields was now looking very
nice, he visited it and saw a lot of residents around there and some wanted to give
the artists some money for the artwork they were doing on the container. There
were also some teenagers excited and telling others that they knew the artists
because they helped them paint the butterflies. They were asking if the artist would
teach them. There was going to be an art class at the teen center that might start
Monday. The artist was going to start his Fernando Valenzuela piece soon and the
Rosewood area was looking good. Community members from Bandini were
requesting for their area to be next to get some of this art. Council Member
Altamirano would like to receive  a presentation to the Council on the Arts in
Public Places account at the next Council meeting.

Council Member Argumedo stated that he was honored to receive the George
Tumanjan Philantropic Award. He provided the history of Mr. Tumanjan and the
Casino with the City of Commerce emphasizing their collaborations to provide for
the Commerce community. He thanked the Commerce Business Council for the
award, city staff, and his colleagues for their support and for attending the event on
Thursday, March 5, 2026. He attended the March 9, 2026 budget session at the
Bandini Library it was a great presentation from the Finance Director.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia attended the neighborhood watch meeting on February 26,
2026 and thanked the Rosewood area residents for attending and voicing their
concerns. She also thanked Public Works Director Abbas and the street
maintenance crew for the work in the Rosewood area. She would like to have more
work done at the Veterans Park area and other parks. She also thanked Public
Safety for the neighborhood watch meeting. She congratulated Council Member
Argumedo on receiving his award. She wished everyone a happy International
Women's Day on March 8.

Mayor Lainez stated he attended the neighborhood watch meeting and thanked
staff for their support and attendance. He stated that he, City Manager Hernandez,
and Community Development Director Serrano attended ICON West a conference

City of Commerce  Page 8  Printed on 5/13/2026
 City Council  Meeting Minutes  March 10, 2026

for industrial real estate. The conference allowed for us to showcase our empty
lots. We received interest from potential businesses. On March 5 he attended the
Commerce Business Council Installation Gala, he congratulated Council Member
Argumedo on receiving his award. He also congratulated the District Manager of
Cal Water, Jim Crawford, who was named President of the Chamber for the fourth
straight year. He attended the LA Kings family hockey trip, Council Member
Argumedo also attended. Although it did not work out for the Kings, it was a great
game. He thanked all the City staff that worked on the coordination, transportation,
and making it a great outing. Mayor Lainez attended the community budget
meeting on March 9th, Director Castellon did a great job presenting the
information. City Manager Hernandez also did a great job explaining the
presentation slides on Measure PC. He congratulated the Commerce Dance Team
for their great showing at the State competition this weekend at Knott's Berry Farm
and wished them luck at nationals.
